summary: Iteration 71 backend testing for Instagram integration scaffold (credentials-empty precondition). 26/26 pytest tests passed (100%). Verified: /api/instagram/status returns {linked:false} for non-linked trainee; oauth/start + oauth/callback return 503 'Instagram integration not yet configured'; /media + /curate return 404 'Instagram not linked' for non-linked user; /refresh returns 503 (configured check happens first — also acceptable per spec); /unlink is idempotent and returns {success:true, deleted:false}; webhooks (GET + POST) /deauthorize and /data-deletion return 200 status:'ok'; data-deletion POST returns Meta-required {url, confirmation_code} shape with the url pointing to /api/privacy/data-deletion-status; /public-media/<random> returns {linked:false, items:[], username:null}; /api/privacy/policy serves HTML (text/html); /api/privacy/data-deletion-status?code=XYZ123 echoes the code in HTML. Regression: /api/auth/login, /api/auth/me, /api/referral/my-code, /api/referral/track-invite, /api/trainers/search?q=test, /api/trainees/search?q=test all pass. No issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: instagram_routes.py: hardcoded host 'https://trainer-finder-9.emergent.host' in data_deletion_webhook URL response (line 480). Should derive from env var (e.g., PUBLIC_BASE_URL or request.base_url) so the link works across preview/prod deployments. Currently the test asserts substring 'data-deletion-status' which passes, but if this host is decommissioned the Meta confirmation link will 404.

instagram_routes.py /refresh: checks _instagram_configured() BEFORE checking if user is linked. For a non-linked user when creds ARE configured, behavior differs vs unconfigured — that's fine, but consider returning 404 'not linked' first to give clearer error to clients regardless of config state. Currently returns 503 in empty-creds env, which is what the test allowed.

instagram_routes.py /oauth/start: writes oauthState to db BEFORE building params — fine, but should also set TTL/expiration on oauthState (currently only oauthStateCreatedAt is recorded; no $expireAfterSeconds index on this field). A stale state could be reused weeks later.

instagram_routes.py /oauth/callback: ig_user_id used as fallback for ig_uid even when profile call returns. If both are missing the link doc would have None for instagramUserId, which then breaks the deauthorize webhook (delete_many would match nothing for that user). Consider validating ig_uid is non-empty before persisting.

instagram_routes.py /data-deletion webhook: generates confirmation_code but does NOT persist it. The /api/privacy/data-deletion-status page accepts ANY ?code= value and echoes it — so the confirmation link is effectively unauthenticated. Acceptable for Meta's reachability check, but if Meta App Review requires verifiable deletion proof, consider storing {code: ig_user_id, deletedAt} for later lookup.
instagram_routes.py: file is well under the 700-line guideline (~490 lines) — no split needed.

instagram_routes.py /public-media/{target_user_id}: requires authentication. If profiles are publicly viewable (Tinder-style swiping inside the app), this is fine; if marketing/web previews need IG grid, would need a separate public endpoint.
